**What this script does.** It checks whether the group effects of ALE from
M5 (04) hold in subsets of countries and country by country.

1. M4 and M5 refitted on the high-income immigrant destination countries
   only, and on the remaining countries.
2. The same five-way model fitted separately in each country (OLS with
   survey weights), and the country effects averaged with every country
   counting equally.

| Output file (in `Results/`) | Content |
|---|---|
| `Robust_destinations_M4.docx/.csv`, `Robust_destinations_M5.docx/.csv` | M4 and M5, high-income destination countries |
| `Robust_other_M5.docx/.csv` | M5, the other countries |
| `Fig_robust_destinations.png`, `Fig_robust_other.png` | Effects of ALE by group, each subset |
| `Fig_robust_by_country.png`, `Robust_by_country.csv` | Country-by-country effects, averaged |

None of these is numbered in the current supplement; the names say what
they contain. All countries in the data are high-income, so the second
subset is "other countries", not "middle-income".

**Input.** `Data/df2.RDS` (01). The random-effects setting is taken from
03 (`Data/models_03.rds`).

## Setup

```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(here)
source(here("R", "load_packages.R"))
source(here("R", "functions_models.R"))

packages <- c("tidyverse", "here", "knitr", "lme4", "performance",
              "flextable", "viridis", "patchwork", "ragg")
load_packages(packages)

df2 <- read_rds(here("Data", "df2.RDS"))
random_part <- read_rds(here("Data", "models_03.rds"))$random_part
stems_all <- c("NFE12", "female", "children", "forlang", "ed3_tertiary", "forborn")
f4 <- make_formula(stems_all, interaction = c("female", "forborn", "children", "forlang", "NFE12"),
                   random = random_part)
f5 <- make_formula(stems_all, interaction = c("female", "forborn", "children", "forlang",
                                              "NFE12", "ed3_tertiary"),
                   random = random_part)
edu_labels <- c("No tertiary degree", "Tertiary degree")
```

## High-income destination countries vs the rest

Within/between parts and their z-scores are recomputed within each subset,
and each country in the subset counts equally.

```{r subsets}
subsets <- list(
  destinations = prep_model_data(df2, intersect(high_income_destinations, unique(df2$iso3c))),
  other        = prep_model_data(df2, setdiff(unique(df2$iso3c), high_income_destinations)))

map(subsets, ~ sort(unique(.x$iso3c)))
map_int(subsets, nrow)
```

```{r subset_models}
m4_dest  <- fit_lmm(f4, subsets$destinations)
m5_dest  <- fit_lmm(f5, subsets$destinations)
m5_other <- fit_lmm(f5, subsets$other)

save_table(model_table(list(M4 = m4_dest)), "Robust_destinations_M4",
           "M4, high-income destination countries")
save_table(model_table(list(M5 = m5_dest)), "Robust_destinations_M5",
           "M5, high-income destination countries")
save_table(model_table(list(M5 = m5_other)), "Robust_other_M5",
           "M5, other countries")
```

```{r subset_effects}
eff_dest  <- profile_ates(m5_dest, subsets$destinations, by_education = TRUE)
eff_other <- profile_ates(m5_other, subsets$other, by_education = TRUE)

save_png(plot_effects(eff_dest, panels = "ed3_tertiary", panel_labels = edu_labels),
         "Fig_robust_destinations.png", width = 1400)
save_png(plot_effects(eff_other, panels = "ed3_tertiary", panel_labels = edu_labels),
         "Fig_robust_other.png", width = 1400)
include_graphics(here("Results", c("Fig_robust_destinations.png", "Fig_robust_other.png")))

bind_rows(destinations = eff_dest, other = eff_other, .id = "subset") %>%
  select(subset, type_id, ed3_tertiary, ATE, se) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = subset, values_from = c(ATE, se)) %>%
  mutate(difference = ATE_destinations - ATE_other,
         se_difference = sqrt(se_destinations^2 + se_other^2)) %>%
  kable(digits = 1)
```

The two subsets are independent samples, so the standard error of the
difference is the square root of the sum of the squared standard errors.
Differences larger than about twice that are unlikely to be chance.

## Country-by-country models

In each country, OLS of literacy on the full five-way interaction of sex,
foreign-born, parenthood, language, ALE and tertiary education, with age
group as a control and the country's survey weights. Each country's group
effects are then averaged across countries (each country counts equally),
with and without the highest and lowest country value. Groups with no
respondents in a country get no effect for that country.

```{r by_country}
d_all <- prep_model_data(df2)
grid <- crossing(ate_profiles, ed3_tertiary = c(0, 1)) %>%
  transmute(type_id, type_label, female, FORBORN = forborn, children,
            FORLANG = forlang, tertiary = ed3_tertiary,
            age_group = factor("35-44", levels = levels(d_all$age_group)))

country_ates <- map_dfr(sort(unique(d_all$iso3c)), function(cc) {
  dc <- filter(d_all, iso3c == cc)
  m  <- lm(skill_reading ~ female * FORBORN * children * FORLANG * NFE12 * tertiary + age_group,
           data = dc, weights = SPFWT0)
  b  <- coef(m)
  # age groups as in this country's model (no "Missing" level where nobody lacks age)
  g  <- mutate(grid, age_group = factor("35-44", levels = m$xlevels$age_group))
  X0 <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(m)), mutate(g, NFE12 = 0))
  X1 <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(m)), mutate(g, NFE12 = 1))
  cdiff <- X1 - X0
  # a group's effect is missing if it needs a coefficient the country cannot estimate
  est <- ifelse(rowSums(cdiff[, is.na(b), drop = FALSE] != 0) > 0, NA,
                cdiff[, !is.na(b), drop = FALSE] %*% b[!is.na(b)])
  mutate(grid, iso3c = cc, ATE = as.numeric(est))
})

trim <- function(x) { x <- sort(na.omit(x)); if (length(x) > 2) x[-c(1, length(x))] else x }

by_country <- country_ates %>%
  group_by(type_id, type_label, ed3_tertiary = tertiary) %>%
  summarise(n_countries = sum(!is.na(ATE)),
            mean = mean(ATE, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(ATE, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_trim = mean(trim(ATE)), sd_trim = sd(trim(ATE)),
            n_trim = length(trim(ATE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ATE = mean_trim,
         se = sd_trim / sqrt(n_trim),
         lower = ATE - qt(0.975, n_trim - 1) * se,
         upper = ATE + qt(0.975, n_trim - 1) * se)

write_csv(by_country %>% mutate(type_label = gsub("\n", " ", type_label)),
          here("Results", "Robust_by_country.csv"))

save_png(plot_effects(by_country, panels = "ed3_tertiary", panel_labels = edu_labels,
                      ylab = "Effect of ALE (mean over countries,\nhighest and lowest dropped)"),
         "Fig_robust_by_country.png", width = 1400)
include_graphics(here("Results", "Fig_robust_by_country.png"))

kable(by_country %>% select(type_id, ed3_tertiary, n_countries, mean, mean_trim, sd), digits = 1)
```

Here the standard error is the spread of the country effects divided by
the square root of the number of countries: it describes how precisely the
average over these countries is known, and the spread itself (`sd`) shows
how much the effect differs between countries.
